Advocate for the Respondent :
 Before
 Honourable Mr. Justice Sanjay Kumar Medhi
 Order
15.03.2024 Heard Shri S.N. Tamuli, learned counsel for the petitioners.

The present challenge is with regard to a Complaint Case being Complaint Case No. CS/97155 of 2023 filed by the respondent no.1 before the 15 th Metropolitan Magistrate, Calcutta under Section 406/420/120 (B)/34 of the Indian Penal Code.

It is the case of the petitioners that they had availed a loan from the respondent no.1 in the year 2017 in connection with which the respondent no. 2 had filed a complaint under Section 138 of the Negotiable Instruments Act, 1881 before the Court of the learned C.J.M., Kamrup (M) and the said case is contested by the petitioners by contending that the cheque in question was misused.

It is submitted that major part of the loan has been repaid and there is no intention at all not to repay the balance part and only to harass the petitioners, the complaint has been filed at Calcutta.

On the aspect of cause of action which has arisen within the jurisdiction of this Court, the learned counsel has submitted that all the transactions were at Sivasagar and the proceeding under the Negotiable Instruments Act is also filed within the State of Assam and therefore, the cause of action has arisen wholly within the jurisdiction of this Court.
Let notice be issued, returnable by 4 (four) weeks.
Page No.# 4/5 Ms. M. Barman, learned State Counsel accepts notice on behalf of the respondent no.
7.

Let steps be taken for service of notice upon the respondent nos. 1 to 6 by registered post with A/D.
Steps within 3 (three) working days.
Shri Tamuli, the learned counsel prays for an interim order.
In support of the plea of there being territorial jurisdiction as there is existence of cause of action within the jurisdiction, the learned counsel has placed reliance upon the following cases.
1. Navinchandra N. Majithia vs. State of Maharashtra & Ors. reported in 2000 7 SCC 640 2.

sentences.text:
In the case of Kusum Ingots (supra), a three judges bench of the Hon'ble Supreme Court by taking into consideration,
Article 226 (2) has made the following observations:
"10.

Keeping in view the expressions used in Clause (2) of Article 226 of the Constitution of India, indisputably even if a small fraction of cause of action accrues within the jurisdiction of the Court, the Court will have jurisdiction in the matter."

On the aspect of the merits of the challenge that the proceeding itself is bad in law, the learned counsel has referred the judgment of Hridaya Ranjan Page No.# 5/5 Pd. Verma & Ors. vs. State of Bihar & Anr. reported in (2000) 4 SCC 168 and has contended that to constitute an offence under Section 420 of the IPC, the intention to deceive has to be there from the very inception.

entities.text: Hridaya Ranjan Page No.# 5/5 Pd. Verma & Ors. vs. State of Bihar & Anr. reported in (2000) 4 SCC 168
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: He submits that payment of a substantial amount by the petitioners itself is a prima facie indication that the petitioners did not have any such intention.

Considering the above, this Court is of the view that interest of justice would be served if further proceedings of Complaint Case No. CS/97155 of 2023 pending in the Court of 15th Metropolitan Magistrate is stayed.

Accordingly, till the returnable date, further proceedings in Complaint Case No. CS/97155 of 2023 pending before the 15th Metropolitan Magistrate under Section 406/420/120 (B)/34 of the Indian Penal Code shall remain stayed.
Since this order has been passed ex-parte, the respondents would be at liberty to file appropriate application for modification of the same.
Cause list to reflect the name of GA, Assam in the cause list.
